title: Ned and the Shy Earwig
checkpoint: Year 1 Spring 1, week 2 — School readiness — Phase 5: new ways to say and spell i, o, o, u
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about earwigs.

pages.text: Ned spots a small bug on the wall top.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling standing on his tiptoes looking at a small reddish-brown bug on top of a stone wall.

pages.text: The bug has sharp points at the back.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the bug showing thin, curved pincers at the tip of its tail.

pages.text: The points look sharp, but they will not hurt.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling leaning in close but calm, looking at the pincers without fear.

pages.text: In the day, the bug hides in a crack in the wall.
pages.illustration: The bug tucked tightly into a narrow dark crack between two stones in the wall.

pages.text: At night, the bug is out to find food.
pages.illustration: The bug emerging from the crack in the wall under a dark night sky with a bright moon.

pages.text: It eats bits of old, soft plants.
pages.illustration: The bug nibbling at a piece of old, soft, curling leaf on the ground.
The bug close to a tiny insect on the stone wall.

pages.text: This bug is not a pest in the garden.
pages.illustration: A clear side view of the whole earwig resting on the flat top of the stone wall.

pages.text: Ned looks as it tucks back into the crack.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling watching as the earwig slips back into the narrow crack in the wall.

pages.text: Ned is glad he spots the shy little bug.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling standing by the wall, looking pleased, the crack with the earwig just visible behind him.
